subject: botany
question_text: An anther has 1200 pollen grains. How many pollen mother cells must have been present to produce them?

mark_split.label: One mother cell gives four grains

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Cell Cycle and Cell Division · 2 marks

steps.label: One mother cell gives four grains
lines: A pollen mother cell, also called a microspore
mother cell, is diploid and divides by meiosis.
One meiosis gives 4 haploid microspores, and
each microspore becomes one pollen grain.
steps.why: Meiosis always gives four products from one cell, and in the anther all four survive as pollen grains. That fixed one-to-four ratio is the whole of this sum.
common_mistakes: Using a ratio of 1 to 2. That is mitosis, not meiosis.
Jumping straight to the number without stating the ratio.
steps.memory_tip: One meiosis, four products. Divide by 4 for mother cells, multiply by 4 for grains.
steps.margin_note: State the ratio in one line before you divide.

steps.label: The answer
steps.why: Divide, do not multiply — the pollen grains are the product and the mother cells are the source. The book writes this as n/4 = 1200/4 = 300 PMC, using n for the number of pollen grains; the arithmetic is right but the symbol is loose, so write 'number of pollen grains ÷ 4' and the examiner can see what you divided.
common_mistakes: Answering 4800 by multiplying instead of dividing.
steps.memory_tip: Grains are more numerous than mother cells, so the answer must be smaller than 1200.
steps.margin_note: One boxed line of arithmetic. Nothing else is needed.

insider_note: The same one-to-four rule answers the megaspore version of this question, except that there only one of the four megaspores stays alive.
